10. Grantee roles and responsibilities

If your application is successful, you will be expected to fulfil the following responsibilities as a grant recipient:

Project delivery

in accepting a grant, you agree that the funds will be spent only on the items, services or activities as laid out in your application and grant offer letter

where stated, MHCLG funding may not be used on specified elements of your application, although you may proceed in the event that additional funding is sourced elsewhere to cover the cost

if circumstances change, and you wish to vary the use of the funds or a proportion of the funds in another way, you must contact Near Neighbours to discuss the situation and seek a variation

Communication and contact

provide a minimum of two named contacts for the project, including telephone numbers and email addresses

ensure that project mailboxes and telephone lines are actively monitored throughout the duration of the grant

if a staff member is absent for longer than 7 days, you must notify Near Neighbours and provide alternative contact details

Monitoring, evaluation and reporting

provide infrequent (verbal) project updates when requested

notify Near Neighbours promptly of any issues, risks, or circumstances that may affect the successful delivery of the project

provide key details of the project activity, including the date, time, venue, and other relevant information

collect and submit participant feedback as requested

complete an impact report (template provided) at the end of the grant funded project.

provide a record of expenditure and supporting evidence (receipts, invoices, or other financial documentation) at the end of the grant funded project

repay any grant funds that have not been spent in accordance with the approved project budget or grant conditions

organisations are required to share copies of project assets (resources) created using funding from the Windrush Day Grant Scheme with MHCLG and Near Neighbours. These materials will form part of a shared archive, including the National Windrush Museum’s Digital Heritage Collection, to help preserve, evidence and showcase the legacy of funded projects

Publicity and promotion

provide us with a post award project summary for use in the Near Neighbours and MHCLG press release, and where appropriate, provide brief event descriptions for inclusion in free-of-charge third-party promotional materials

any publicity material for the funded activities must refer to the Windrush Day Grant Scheme under which the Grant was awarded and must feature the MHCLG logo

it is expected you would tag Near Neighbours and MHCLG on social media when sharing content about the funded project

when providing us (MHCLG, Church Urban Fund, Near Neighbours and partners) with any photographs you would ensure that the necessary consents have been provided and that we are granted permission to make use of the images

Compliance

operate in accordance with all relevant legislation, policies, and safeguarding requirements

grant-funded projects must refrain from engaging in political activity

all grant recipients are required to ensure that all aspects of their project benefiting from grant funding maintain a politically impartial stance throughout. Projects must not espouse or imply any partisan political views

11. Timeline

Application window opens: 1 October 2026

Bidder’s workshops: 9 to 20 October 2026

Application window closes: 23:59 29 October 2026

Panel meetings: January 2027

Departmental checks and sign off: February 2027

Applicants notified of application outcome: March 2027

Subject to the return of signed grant agreements from successful applicants, funding distributed to projects: April 2027

National Windrush Day: 22 June 2027

Funding period ends (all projects must complete activity by this date): 31 July 2027

Reporting due date: 31 August 27

Near Neighbours will be hosting bidder workshops to provide an overview of the scheme and offer bidders a chance to ask questions.

The workshops will be held virtually on:

Friday 9 October 11:00am to 12:00pm

Tuesday 13 October 11:00am to 12:00pm

Wednesday 14 October 06:00pm to 07:00pm

Tuesday 20 October 06:00pm to 07:00pm

Please register here to attend

12. How to apply

This grants programme is administered by Church Urban Fund, through its Near Neighbours programme, on behalf of MHCLG.

You can apply to the scheme via the application form on our administrator Church Urban Fund, website.

Applications must be submitted by 23:59 on 29 October 2026.

Please direct any queries relating to the grant scheme and the application process to our external administrator Near Neighbours at windrush@cuf.org.uk

You can access MHCLG’s privacy notice which sets out the standards you can expect us to meet when we ask for, do something with or continue to hold, your personal information. It also covers what we ask of you, to help us keep information up to date.

13. Definitions

Charity – a registered charity with a UK charity number or a registered CIC (community interest company).

Community group – a group that meets all the following criteria:

established for charitable, benevolent or philanthropic purposes

has a governing body with at least three members

has a governing document which they are able to produce

can provide accounts for the last 2 financial years

NB: Individuals are not eligible to apply but should work with groups as set out above.
